LESSON: VEGETATION IN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 4.3: Vegetation in Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Vegetation in Africa, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we care for vegetation in our environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm in groups factors influencing vegetation in Africa and do a presentation in class, learners with speech difficulties

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm in groups factors influencing vegetation in Africa and do a presentation in class, learners with speech difficulties

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Vegetation in Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: Learners speak clearly during debate on importance of vegetation in the community.

● Citizenship: Learners enhance skills of caring for the environment when creating posters on methods of conserving

vegetation in the locality.

● Digital Literacy: Learners use digital devices to accomplish the task of finding out the vegetation regions in Africa.

Values:
● Unity: Learners display team spirit when carrying out a field excursion of the immediate environment to identify the

different types of vegetation.

● Responsibility: Learners accomplish the task of finding out the vegetation regions in Africa.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education: Learners participate in debating on the importance of vegetation in the community.

Link to other subjects:

● The learner applies skills from Agriculture and Nutrition as they discuss methods of conserving vegetation in the locality.
